messages:
sophie: Heads-up - Support forwarded a customer report: several requests to the hosted /v1/generate endpoint are getting 502s. They should be getting 429 for quota exceeded. Customer says it started ~10:15 UTC. pinging infra and eng.

jen-support: Customer: jdoe@acme.com, org id org_82. Reports spike of 502s at 10:14-10:19 UTC, about ~120 failures. Provided request id samples: req_4f3b, req_4f3c. They pasted a curl: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-1","input":"hi"}'`

ops-bot: [incident-detect] alert triggered: high-5xx-rate for service=ratecheck-proxy, window=5m, threshold=0.02 -> 0.09.

alex: I'm seeing the same in SLO dashboard: upstream 502 spike from ratecheck-proxy -> quota-orch. Latency to quota backend jumped and then a subset of calls returned 502 rather than 429.

liz: grabbing logs from ratecheck-proxy for those request ids now. May be a misroute to our maintenance backend.

alex: quick theory: quota service dependency (auth-cache or token-refresher) timed out, and proxy mapped dependency timeout to 502 instead of converting to 429. Need reproduction.

sophie: agree. This is customer-facing: 429 should be surfaced when a request is denied due to quota. 502 indicates server error and causes alerts/escalations.

liz: logs snippet for req_4f3b (sanitized):

```
[2025-11-04T10:15:12.345Z] ratecheck-proxy req=req_4f3b -> route=quota-orch cluster=quota-prod-1
[2025-11-04T10:15:12.678Z] upstream call timeout after 5000ms: target=quota-orch-primary
[2025-11-04T10:15:12.679Z] error mapping: upstream timeout -> return_code=502
[2025-11-04T10:15:12.679Z] fallback attempted: route=quota-orch-secondary -> success=false
[2025-11-04T10:15:12.680Z] final_response=502
```

jen-support: The customer is pretty unhappy; they saw their app autoretry logic treat 502 differently. Ask for mitigation steps.

tim: Immediate mitigation: update proxy mapping to treat quota-orch timeout as 429 if the original intent was deny. We can flip mapping in runtime config (route policy) to return 429 on specific error codes from quota-orch in the next 2-3 minutes. I can push a gate.

alex: Before we change mapping, we should confirm the root cause. If quota-orch was overloaded and couldn't make decision, returning 429 might be wrong if we can't verify quota (could be under-acknowledged). But agreed surface mapping should be 4xx for quota denies.

liz: Checking quota-orch metrics: rolling CPU spike on quota-orch-primary at 10:14:54, memory ok, connection pool exhaustion to auth-cache. auth-cache region eu-west had a transient GC at 10:14:50 and opened up at 10:16:00. So quota-orch timed out waiting for auth-cache and returned internal error.

sophie: So chain: auth-cache GC -> quota-orch dependency timeout -> quota-orch returned 500-ish -> proxy treated as upstream 5xx -> turned into 502 to customers. This is the misroute.

jen-support: Customer requested repro steps. Can we produce minimal repro that we can run safely?

tim: Repro plan (dev env): 1) point ratecheck-proxy at a quota-orch dev instance with a simulated auth-cache delay; 2) issue concurrent requests until the quota code path hits the auth-cache call; 3) confirm proxy returns 502 when quota-orch returns 500 due to dependency timeout; 4) confirm mapping change results in 429.

alex: Example curl to reproduce locally (do NOT run against prod):

```
# against dev cluster with injected delay
for i in {1..50}; do \
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
    "https://dev-api.redwood.local/v1/generate?simulate_auth_delay=6000" &
done
wait
```

liz: I patched dev quota-orch to simulate auth-cache latency and confirmed proxy returned 502 for ~20% of requests while quota-orch returned 500. After changing proxy error mapping in dev to map quota-orch timeout->429, customer-visible returned code switched to 429.

sophie: Action items:
- liz: produce an RCA draft explaining auth-cache GC -> quota-orch timeout -> proxy misroute (deadline EOD).
- tim: prepare a safe runtime config change to map timeouts from quota-orch to 429 (canary to 5% traffic) and a rollback plan.
- alex: coordinate with runtime and infra to verify no other subsystems rely on 502 for internal flows.
- jen-support: inform customer about planned fix and temporary mitigations.

jen-support: I'll tell customer we have a mitigations plan and a canary rolling in ~30m. I asked for their acceptance to run a canary; they approved.

ops-bot: [deploy] runtime-config change queued: change_id rc_20251104_01, target=ratecheck-proxy, strategy=canary(5%). Owner=tim.

tim: Pushing a config snippet to change mapping (will roll canary):

```
# ratecheck-proxy error mapping (yaml)
routes:
  - match: path_prefix(/v1/generate)
    upstream_errors:
      quota-orch-timeout: return_status: 429
```

alex: After canary started we saw customer 502s drop by 80% and 429 increase accordingly. Monitoring shows no increase in customer retries or downstream errors.

liz: Quota-orch team will work on auth-cache stability and add defensive timeouts and circuit-breakers so a dependency GC doesn't cascade.

sophie: Long-term: add invariants that quota-orch must return canonical 4xx when the decision is a deny; if decision cannot be made, it should return a specific transient code we map to a safe customer-facing 429 with an explanatory header. Add tests for mapping.

customer-jdoe: Thanks for fast response. The canary fixed it for us, but please keep us updated on root cause and ETA to full fix.

jen-support: Noted. I'll send a follow-up email with timeline and next steps.

sophie: Closing loop: assign RCA doc to liz and mark incident P2. Will turn this into a postmortem if customer impact widens. :thumbsup:

alex: +1. Adding retrospective item: add synthetic checks for mapping regressions and a small test harness that simulates dependency latency so mapping logic cannot regress without alerting.

ops-bot: [incident-close-proposal] suggested severity=P2, start=1723456789, end=1723457020, owner=sophie.

sophie: thanks everyone. If anything else pops up, update this thread.
